title: Project financing in vanishing forests: Do investors care about nature protection?
abstract: arXiv:2611.29281v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Biodiversity risks are increasingly recognized by financial market participants, yet their measurement at the corporate-entity level obscures the locations and assets through which they arise. Project finance links identifiable physical assets to dedicated financing contracts, allowing us to examine this transmission more directly. By linking 9,037 project-loan pairs in 115 countries, we relate bank loan spreads to projects' proximity to protected areas, surrounding forest loss and lenders' nature policies. We find that lenders price proximity to protected areas only when they also have explicit nature risk policies and particularly within 1.5 km buffers from the project location. Realised forest loss around a project is priced more consistently than forest loss after the loan is signed, and risk pricing near protected areas strengthens after the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. translated_title: 消失森林中的项目融资：投资者在乎自然保护吗？
translated_abstract: 生物多样性风险日益受到金融市场参与者的重视，然而在企业实体层面的风险度量掩盖了这些风险产生的具体地点和资产。项目融资将可识别的实体资产与专门的融资合同联系起来，使我们能够更直接地考察这种风险传导机制。通过关联115个国家的9,037个项目-贷款配对，我们将银行贷款利差与项目距离保护区的远近、项目周边的森林损失以及贷款机构的自然保护政策联系起来。我们发现，只有当贷款机构自身也拥有明确的自然风险政策时，才会对项目靠近保护区的程度进行定价，且主要体现在项目位置1.5公里缓冲区范围内。项目周边已实际发生的森林损失比贷款签署之后发生的森林损失被定价得更为一致，而在《昆明-蒙特利尔全球生物多样性框架》通过之后，保护区附近的风险定价进一步增强。上市公司作为项目赞助方也会承受负面（影响）……
tldr: 银行只有在自身具备明确的自然风险政策时，才会对靠近保护区（尤其是1.5公里范围内）及周边发生森林损失的项目收取更高的贷款利差，且这种风险定价在《昆明-蒙特利尔全球生物多样性框架》通过后进一步增强。
en_tdlr: Banks price higher loan spreads for projects near protected areas—especially within a 1.5 km buffer—and for realized forest loss, but only when lenders have explicit nature risk policies, and this pricing intensified after the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
